fairness_call: HOLDS - for all n and all 0 <= k <= n. The mechanism named in the abstract is the classical Polya urn with one ball per value and unit reinforcement, whose composition distribution is uniform over multisets; composed with a bijection, uniformity is preserved exactly. If the paper falls, the seal expects it to fall on a discrepancy between the described mechanism and the specified or implemented one (an off-by-one in t = n-k+1 or in the stars-and-bars conversion), not on the mechanism itself.

shape: A reduction. Cardchoose moves the uniformity burden from k-subsets - hard to sample directly without rejection, extra memory, or floating-point arithmetic - onto multisets of size k drawn from n-k+1 values, where a classical reinforcement process (Polya's urn: each draw adds a copy of the drawn value) makes every composition equally likely. The stars-and-bars bijection then transfers uniformity from multisets to k-subsets exactly, being a bijection between two spaces of the same size C(n,k). The algorithm is the composition: urn, sort, shift. The rest of the paper is an engineering argument that this reduction is also fast, memory-free, and simple across the whole (n,k) range, benchmarked against twelve other algorithms in two languages.
title: Cardchoose: simple, fast sampling without replacement
